title: One Linear Regression Step
statement: Implement `linreg_step(w, x, y, lr)` for one example of linear regression without a separate bias feature (put a constant 1 in x if you want a bias). Prediction is the dot product of w and x. Update each weight by subtracting lr times (prediction − y) times the matching x coordinate. Return the new weight vector. This is gradient descent on half the squared error.
constraints: Return a new list; do not require the caller to reuse the old one

approaches.name: SGD on half-square loss
approaches.explanation: One example, one step. Full-batch GD averages this gradient over the dataset.

editorial: For a single row, loss L = 0.5 (w · x − y)² has gradient (w · x − y) x. Subtracting learning-rate times that gradient is stochastic gradient descent. The leading 0.5 is a convention so the 2 from the chain rule disappears; some texts omit it and fold the 2 into the learning rate. State which convention you use. A bias term is just a feature that is always 1, which is why this signature has no separate intercept.
reference_solution:
def linreg_step(w: list[float], x: list[float], y: float, lr: float) -> list[float]:
    pred = sum(wi * xi for wi, xi in zip(w, x))
    err = pred - y
    return [wi - lr * err * xi for wi, xi in zip(w, x)]
